subject: RFP: reserve pool orchestration and GPU family mapping
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@nimbusai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbusai.com
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Dedicated inference reserve + GPU family mapping (NimbusAI)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Attached is our questionnaire (nimbus_rfp_dedicated_questionnaire_v2.xlsx) and a short summary of our targets:

- Workload: LLM serving for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) + multi-turn chat. Primary model family target: Llama-3-70B (fp16 baseline) with quantized fallbacks.
- Traffic profile: steady-state ~120 req/s (avg prompt+generation ~512 tokens), burst up to 250 req/s for up to 30 minutes during peak events.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation <= 200ms for responses <= 1024 tokens. p50 obviously much lower.
- Availability: 99.95% monthly, with automatic fallback to lower-cost variants if capacity constrained.
- Security/compliance notes: customer data stays in our VPC; we need audit logs and KMS integration.

Questions for the vendor:
1) Recommended GPU families and a reserve-plan (how many reserved nodes vs. on-demand burst lanes) to hit the targets above.
2) Expected per-GPU throughput (req/s) for the model family in fp16 and in 4-bit quantized variants.
3) Warm-up behavior: cold-start to steady KV-cache hit-rate for RAG (how long until full cache benefits).
4) Fallback and routing: how you would orchestrate automatic fallbacks between families/quantizations.
5) Pricing structure for committed reservations (monthly vs annual) and burst rates.

Can you get a completed response back in 48 hours? We have an internal procurement window that closes next week.

Thanks,
Asha Rao
Head of Procurement
NimbusAI

Attachments: nimbus_rfp_dedicated_questionnaire_v2.xlsx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@nimbusai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated inference reserve + GPU family mapping (NimbusAI)

Hi Asha — appreciate the clear targets and the questionnaire. High-level answers and a recommended reserve plan are attached (redwood_gpu_mapping.xlsx and redwood_rfp_response.pdf). TL;DR below; full workbook has test assumptions and per-model perf numbers.

TL;DR recommendation (short):
- Primary reserved fleet: 12 x H100-80GB nodes (shared single-tenant pool) configured for fp16 Llama-3-70B serving. This gives steady-state headroom for ~140 req/s with p95 ~160ms for <=1024-token responses under our benchmarks (continuous batching + KV caching enabled).
- Burst lane: 4 H100 nodes (burstable, not reserved) and 8 A100-80GB nodes in a quantized capacity tier. Under extreme events we route low-latency traffic first to reserved H100s and spill to quantized A100s for degraded-but-cost-effective throughput.
- Alt mix (cost-sensitive): 24 A100-80GB reserved using int8/4-bit quantized models — this meets burst targets but will increase tail latency (p95 ~260ms) for large responses; recommended only if budget constraints are primary.
- Fallback policy: policy-based routing (latency-first) + automatic quantization promotion when queue depth > 60% for reserved H100s. Canary for any model variant changes with automatic rollback after regression threshold.

Notes on throughput:
- H100-80GB (fp16 L3-70B): ~12-14 req/s per GPU for 512-token average generation with continuous batching and KV-cache warming.
- A100-80GB (int8/4-bit quant): ~7-9 req/s per GPU for same workload. Exact numbers in workbook (sheet: perf-assumptions).

Warm-up behavior and KV cache:
- Cold start: initial requests experience ~2x latency and lower effective throughput until KV caches warm. For typical RAG setups we see cache stabilization (80% effective hit-rate) after ~5-12 minutes depending on working set size and prefix reuse. We recommend a short prewarm window (scripted prefix replay) during release and a short-lived standby lane to absorb the ramp.

Operational controls:
- Autoscale guardrails: target queue depth thresholds, preemptive spin-up for scheduled events, and burst-lane throttles.
- Tracing & audit: per-token tracing hooks, write-once audit logs integrated with KMS, S3 retention per your compliance note.

Next steps:
1) We can run a tailored load test (48-hour window) using your sample prompts to validate model/quantization mix and finalize reserved counts.
2) If agreeable, we’ll deliver a draft pricing worksheet (monthly and annual reserved pricing tiers + burst rates) and an SLA appendix.

Attachments: redwood_gpu_mapping.xlsx, redwood_rfp_response.pdf

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Rishi / Karthik —

Nice summary. A couple of internal asks before we send pricing:
- Can we get the load-test plan skeleton and estimated duration (I want us to commit to a single validated throughput number we can include in the quote). I attached a short plan (loadtest-plan.md) with phases: smoke, steady-state, stress.
- Pricing guidance: what tiered discount bands apply at 12 vs 24 vs 36-month commitments and whether we can include an upfront credit for multi-year. Also call out any marketplace discounts if they bring a cloud-reseller commitment.
- Confirm the fallback latency impact numbers we put in the proposal (we should avoid promising p95 <=200ms if using A100 quantized fallback; instead show p95 ~250-275ms).

We should get a draft pricing worksheet ready before EOD tomorrow so procurement has something to review. Rishi — can you own the technical appendices? Karthik — can you pull preliminary pricing bands and a rough ARR calc?

Thanks,
Laura
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Rishi — thanks for the fast turnaround and the workbook. A few clarifications from procurement and infra before we proceed:

1) Cold-start/warm-up: your 5-12 minute warm-up estimate — can you provide an expected warm-up delta (warm vs cold p95) for our ops team to size buffer lanes? Example: cold p95 is 380ms, warm p95 160ms for a 512-token gen.
2) Contract terms: can you provide a simple anchor for monthly committed spend for the recommended plan (12 H100 reserved + 4 burst H100 + 8 A100 burst)? We need a ballpark to present in the pricing committee.
3) Do you support a managed prewarm job as part of onboarding (we’d like to incorporate it into cutover runbook)? If so, is that a one-time professional-service task or part of the Dedicated plan?

Procurement calendar attached (nimbus_procurement_calendar.pdf). If you can provide the warm-up delta and a ballpark committed monthly cost by EOD Friday, we can prioritize Redwood for the award.

Regards,
Asha Rao
Head of Procurement
NimbusAI
